八背捨 · 釋名 · 次位 · 觀法不同

zh: 二、背捨者，壞內色，滅內色相，不壞外色，不滅外色相，以是不淨心觀外色，是第二背捨。所以者何？行者於初背捨中，骨人放光既遍，今欲入二禪內淨故，壞滅內骨人，取盡欲界見思未斷故，猶觀外白骨不淨之相，故云以是不淨心觀外色。今明修證。行者於初背捨後心中，不受覺觀動亂，諦觀內身骨人虛假不實，內外空疎，專取壞散磨滅之相。如是觀時，漸漸見於骨人腐爛碎壞，猶如塵粉，散滅歸空，不見內色，是時但攝心入定，緣外光明及與不淨，一心緣中，不受觀覺，於後內心豁然明淨，三昧正受與大喜俱發，即見八種光明照從內淨，出明十方，倍勝於上。既證內法大喜光明，即知根本二禪虛誑麁劣，厭背不著，故名背捨，亦名無漏第二禪。是中具有四支，推尋可見。
en: Second, the second detachment: destroying internal form, extinguishing the mark of internal form, while not destroying external form, nor extinguishing the mark of external form — using this impure mind to contemplate external form: this is the second detachment. Why is this? The practitioner, within the first detachment, the figure of bone already radiating light everywhere, now wishing to enter the second dhyāna's own internal purity, thereby destroys and extinguishes the internal figure of bone; yet, since the views and thoughts belonging to the desire realm are not yet entirely severed, one still contemplates the external mark of white bone's own impurity — hence it is said: using this impure mind, one contemplates external form.

Now, clarifying cultivation and realization: the practitioner, in the mind following the first detachment, no longer accepting initial thought and sustained reflection's own agitation and disturbance, closely contemplates that the internal figure of bone is empty and unreal, both internal and external hollow and sparse, taking up exclusively the mark of its own destruction, scattering, and dissolution. Contemplating in this way, one gradually sees the figure of bone rotting away and crumbling apart, like dust and powder, scattering into nothing and returning to emptiness — the internal form no longer seen at all. At this time, one simply gathers the mind and enters concentration, taking the external light together with impurity as one's object, the mind fixed one-pointedly upon it, no longer accepting sustained reflection and initial thought. Afterward, the internal mind opens out, bright and pure, right samādhi arising together with great joy — one then sees the eight kinds of light shining forth from this internal purity, illuminating the ten directions, doubly surpassing what was obtained before. Having realized this internal dharma's own great joy and radiance, one thereby knows that the root second dhyāna is itself empty and illusory, coarse and inferior, and turns away from it in weariness, no longer attached to it — hence this is named detachment, also named the undefiled second dhyāna. Within this, the four factors are complete, and may be found through careful inquiry.

zh: 三、淨背捨身作證者，如《摩訶衍》中說：「緣淨故淨，遍身受樂，故名身作證。」所以者何？行者欲入是三背捨，於二背捨後，心即不受，觀外不淨，悉皆壞盡散滅，無有遺餘，亦不受大喜勇動，但攝心諦觀八色光耀之相。取是相已，入深三昧，鍊此八色，極令明淨，住心緣中，即泯然入定。定發之時，與樂俱生，見外八色光明清淨皎潔，猶如妙寶光色，各隨其想，昱晃明照，遍滿諸方，外徹清淨，外色照心，心即明淨，樂漸增長，遍滿身中，舉體怡悅。既證此法，背捨根本，心不樂著。是則略說證淨背捨相，亦名無漏三禪。是中具足五支，深思可見，乃至四禪淨色亦復如是，皆淨背捨所攝，但以無遍身樂為異耳。
en: Third, the pure detachment realized in the body: as explained in the Mahāyāna treatise, "Taking purity as its object, one is thereby pure; the whole body receiving happiness — hence this is named realization in the body." Why is this? The practitioner, wishing to enter this third detachment, following the second detachment, the mind no longer accepting the contemplation of external impurity, which has, in every case, already been utterly destroyed, scattered, and dissolved, nothing whatsoever remaining, and no longer accepting the great joy's own excited agitation either — simply gathers the mind and closely contemplates the mark of the eight colors' own radiance. Taking up this mark, one enters a deep samādhi, refining these eight colors until they grow utterly bright and pure, the mind resting fixed upon this very object, and thereupon settles, undisturbed, into concentration.

At the moment concentration arises, happiness is born together with it — one sees the eight external colors of light, pure and radiantly clear, like the color of some wondrous jewel's own light, each following its own mental image, shining and brilliantly illuminating, spreading throughout every direction, its own purity penetrating outward; this external color illuminates the mind, and the mind thereby grows bright and pure, happiness gradually increasing, spreading throughout the whole body, the entire body filled with delight. Having realized this dharma, one turns away from the root dhyāna, the mind no longer taking delight in or attaching to it. This, then, briefly explains the mark of realizing the pure detachment, also named the undefiled third dhyāna. Within this, the five factors are complete, and may be found through deep reflection; and, further still, the fourth dhyāna's own pure color is likewise so, equally included within the pure detachment, differing only in that happiness no longer pervades the whole body there.

zh: 問曰：若爾，從初背捨來，悉有淨色，何故今方說為淨背捨耶？答曰：是中應用四義分別：一者、不淨不淨；二者、不淨淨；三者、淨不淨；四者、淨淨不淨。不淨者，如欲界三十六物之身性相已是不淨。不淨觀力，更見此身胮脹、膿爛、青瘀、臭處，此則不淨中更見不淨。不淨淨者，如白骨本是不淨之體，諦心觀之，膏膩既盡，如珂如貝，白光焴爍，此則不淨中淨也。
en: Question: if this is so, from the very first detachment onward, pure color has already been present — why, then, is it only now that this is spoken of as the pure detachment? Answer: within this, four senses should be applied in distinguishing it: first, the impure-impure; second, the impure-pure; third, the pure-impure; fourth, the pure-pure.

As for the impure: such as the desire realm's own thirty-six substances, whose bodily nature and mark are already impure. Through the power of the contemplation of impurity, one further sees this very body swollen, festering, livid, and foul — this is impurity seen further within impurity itself. As for the impure-pure: such as the white bone, itself originally an impure substance; closely contemplating it, once its grease and residue are entirely gone, it becomes like agate, like shell, its white light shimmering — this is purity found within impurity.

zh: 淨中不淨者，從初背捨來，雖有淨光，但此光明有三種不淨因緣：一者、出處不淨，謂從骨人出也；二者、所照不淨，謂照外境也；三者、光體未被鍊故不淨，譬如金不被鍊，滓穢未盡，光色不淨。以是因緣，初禪雖有光明，不名緣淨故淨；二禪雖無白骨，光從內淨而出，猶照外不淨，而未被鍊，及大喜故，亦得名為緣淨。今言淨淨者，八色光明本是淨色，今於此地又離三種不淨，故淨言淨淨，亦名緣淨故淨。既淨義具足，所以說為淨背捨也。
en: As for the pure-impure: from the very first detachment onward, though pure light is already present, this very light bears three kinds of impure cause and condition: first, its place of origin is impure, since it issues from the figure of bone itself; second, that which it illuminates is impure, since it illuminates external objects; third, the light's own substance has not yet been refined, and is thus impure — like gold not yet refined, its dross and impurity not yet exhausted, its own light and color impure. For causes and conditions such as these, though the first dhyāna already possesses light, it is not yet named taking purity as its object and thereby being pure; the second dhyāna, though free of white bone, its light issuing from internal purity itself, still illuminates external impurity, and has not yet been refined — and, on account of the great joy present there as well, this, too, may be named taking purity as its object.

As for what is now spoken of as the pure-pure: the eight colors of light are, in their origin, already pure color; here, at this very stage, they are, further, freed of all three kinds of impurity — hence this purity is spoken of as pure-pure, also named taking purity as its object and thereby being pure. The sense of purity now being entirely complete, this is, for this reason, spoken of as the pure detachment.

The four-fold impure/pure analysis (impure-impure, impure-pure, pure-impure, pure-pure) is a good example of this treatise's characteristic move of refusing binary categories in favor of a graded matrix — "purity" turns out to have its own internal impurities (where the light comes from, what it illuminates, whether it has been refined) that must themselves be resolved in sequence before the third detachment can rightfully claim the name. The three grounds for the earlier detachments' light still counting as merely "pure-impure" — tainted origin (the first detachment's light issuing from the figure of bone), tainted object, un-refined substance — read almost like a chemistry of spiritual attainment, each impurity requiring a specific, separate purification before the next stage becomes available.

八背捨 · 釋名 · 次位 · 觀法不同

zh: 四、虛空背捨者，行者於欲界後，已除自身皮肉不淨之色；初背捨後，已滅內身白骨之色；二背捨後，已却外一切不淨之色，唯有八種淨色至第四禪。此八種色皆依心住，譬如幻色，依幻心住，若心捨色，色即謝滅。一心緣空，與空相應，即入無邊虛空處，此明滅色方便異於前也。證虛空處定，義如前說。
en: Fourth, the detachment of the sphere of space: the practitioner, after the desire realm, has already removed the impure color of the skin and flesh of his own body; after the first detachment, has already extinguished the internal body's own color of white bone; after the second detachment, has already set aside every impure external color as well, leaving only the eight kinds of pure color, all the way up through the fourth dhyāna. These eight colors, all alike, rest dependent upon the mind — like an illusory color, dependent upon an illusory mind; should the mind relinquish this color, the color thereupon fades and vanishes. The mind fixed one-pointedly upon space, corresponding with space itself, one thereby enters the boundless sphere of space — this clarifies a skillful means for extinguishing color that differs from what came before. Realizing the concentration of the sphere of space follows the same sense as already explained above.

zh: 行者欲入虛空背捨，當先入空定。空定即是背捨之初門，背捨色緣無色故。凡夫人入此定，名為無色；佛弟子入此定，深心一向不迴，是名背捨。云何名深心？善修奢摩他故。云何名一向不迴？於此定中，善修毘婆舍那、空、無相、無作、無願故，能捨根本著心，即不退沒，輪轉生死，故名一向不迴。復次，佛弟子當入無色定時，即有八聖種觀。如癰瘡等四種對治觀故，即能厭背無色之法；無常等四種正觀故，即破無色假、實二倒，能發無漏。八聖種觀行方法，並如前離虛空定，修識定時說。但彼欲離虛空故，方修八聖種，今行人即入虛空定時，即修八聖種，雖住定中，而不著虛空定，故名背捨也。五、識處；六、無所有處；七、非有想非無想處背捨，亦當如是一一分別。
en: The practitioner, wishing to enter the detachment of the sphere of space, should first enter the concentration on space. The concentration on space is precisely the initial gate of detachment, since detachment turns away from form and takes the formless as its object. The ordinary person entering this concentration, this is named formlessness; the Buddha's disciple entering this concentration, the deep mind turned wholly in one direction, never turning back — this is named detachment. What is meant by "the deep mind"? Skillfully cultivating calming. What is meant by "turned wholly in one direction, never turning back"? Within this concentration, skillfully cultivating insight, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and no-action, one is thereby able to relinquish the root's own attached mind, and thereupon never again retreats or sinks back, turning through the wheel of birth-and-death — hence this is named turned wholly in one direction, never turning back.

Furthermore, when the Buddha's disciple is about to enter the formless concentration, the eight noble lineages' own contemplation is present as well. Through the four kinds of antidote-contemplation, such as seeing it as a boil or a wound, one is thereby able to grow weary of and turn away from the formless dharma; through the four kinds of correct contemplation, such as impermanence, one thereby breaks through the two inversions of the formless — provisional and real — and is able to give rise to the undefiled. The method of the eight noble lineages' own contemplative practice is entirely as already explained above, at the point of departing from the concentration of space and cultivating the concentration of consciousness. It is only that, there, one wishes to depart from the sphere of space, and so cultivates the eight noble lineages for that purpose; here, the practitioner, at the very moment of entering the concentration of space, already cultivates the eight noble lineages — though abiding within the concentration, one is not attached to the concentration of space itself, hence this is named detachment.

Fifth, the detachment of the sphere of consciousness; sixth, the detachment of the sphere of nothingness; seventh, the detachment of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — these, too, should each in turn be distinguished in just this same way.

zh: 八、滅受想背捨者，背滅受、想諸心心數法，是名滅受想背捨。所以者何？諸佛弟子厭患散亂心故，入定休息，似涅槃法，安著身中，故名身證。行者修是滅受想背捨，必須滅非想陰界入及諸心數法。云何滅？是非想中雖無麁煩惱，而具足四陰、二入、三界、十種細心數法，所謂：一、受；二、想；三、行；四、觸；五、思；六、欲；七、解；八、念；九、定；十、慧。云何為受？所謂識受。云何為想？所謂識想。云何為行？所謂法行。云何為觸？所謂意觸。云何為思？所謂法思。云何為欲？謂入出定。云何為解？所謂法解。云何為念？謂念於三昧。云何為定？謂心如法住。云何為慧？謂慧根。慧身及無色愛、無明、掉慢心、不相應諸行等苦集法和合因緣，則有非想。
en: Eighth, the detachment of the cessation of sensation and perception: turning away from and extinguishing sensation, perception, and every mental factor of the mind — this is named the detachment of the cessation of sensation and perception. Why is this? Every disciple of the Buddha, wearying of the scattered and disordered mind, enters concentration to rest, a dharma resembling nirvāṇa itself, settling securely within the body — hence this is named realization in the body.

The practitioner cultivating this detachment of the cessation of sensation and perception must extinguish the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases belonging to neither-perception-nor-non-perception, together with every mental factor. How does one extinguish them? Within this neither-perception-nor-non-perception, though free of coarse affliction, one is nonetheless complete with four aggregates, two sense-bases, three elements, and ten kinds of subtle mental factors, namely: first, sensation; second, perception; third, formation; fourth, contact; fifth, intention; sixth, desire; seventh, resolve; eighth, mindfulness; ninth, concentration; tenth, wisdom.

What is sensation? Namely, the sensation belonging to consciousness. What is perception? Namely, the perception belonging to consciousness. What is formation? Namely, the formation belonging to dharmas. What is contact? Namely, mental contact. What is intention? Namely, intention toward dharmas. What is desire? Namely, the wish to enter and leave concentration. What is resolve? Namely, resolve regarding dharmas. What is mindfulness? Namely, mindfulness of samādhi itself. What is concentration? Namely, the mind abiding in accordance with the dharma. What is wisdom? Namely, the faculty of wisdom. The body of wisdom, together with craving for the formless realm, ignorance, the agitated and conceited mind, and the dissociated formations and the rest — through the coming together of causes and conditions belonging to the truth of suffering and its accumulation — neither-perception-nor-non-perception thereby comes to be.

zh: 前於非想背捨中，雖知是事，不著非想，故名背捨，而未滅諸心數法。今行者欲入滅受想背捨故，必須不受非想，一心緣真，絕陰界入，則非想陰入界滅，一切諸行因緣悉滅，受滅乃至慧滅，愛、無明等諸煩惱滅，一切心數法滅，一切非心數亦滅，是名不與凡夫共，非是世法。若能如是觀者，是名滅受想。以能觀真之受想，滅非想苦集之受想。今行者欲入滅受想之背捨，復須深知能觀真之受想亦非究竟寂靜，即捨能觀之定受慧想。捨此緣真定、慧二心，故云背滅受想諸心數法。譬如以後聲止前聲，前聲既息，即後聲亦如是能除。受想既息，因此心與滅法相應，滅法持心，寂然無所知覺，故云身證想受滅。此定中既無心識，若欲出入，但聽本要期長短也。
en: In the earlier detachment of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, though this matter was already known, one was not attached to neither-perception-nor-non-perception — hence this, too, was named detachment — but the mental factors themselves had not yet been extinguished. Now, the practitioner wishing to enter the detachment of the cessation of sensation and perception must no longer accept neither-perception-nor-non-perception at all, the mind fixed one-pointedly upon reality itself, cutting off the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases entirely — the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements belonging to neither-perception-nor-non-perception are thereby extinguished, every conditioned formation's own causes and conditions entirely extinguished, sensation extinguished, and, further still, wisdom itself extinguished, craving, ignorance, and every other affliction extinguished, every mental factor extinguished, and every non-mental factor, too, extinguished — this is named "not shared in common with the ordinary person," not a worldly dharma at all. Should one be able to contemplate in this way, this is named the cessation of sensation and perception, using the sensation and perception that are able to contemplate reality itself to extinguish the sensation and perception belonging to the suffering and accumulation of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Now, the practitioner wishing to enter this very detachment of the cessation of sensation and perception must, further, deeply know that even the sensation and perception able to contemplate reality are not themselves the ultimate stillness, and must thereupon relinquish the very concentration-sensation and wisdom-perception that are able to contemplate. Relinquishing these two minds of concentration and wisdom that take reality as their object — hence it is said: turning away from and extinguishing sensation, perception, and every mental factor. It is like using a later sound to still an earlier sound: the earlier sound having already ceased, the later sound, too, is able to be removed in just the same way. Sensation and perception having already ceased, the mind, on account of this, corresponds with the dharma of cessation itself; the dharma of cessation holds the mind fast, still and silent, without any awareness or perception at all — hence it is said: realization in the body of the cessation of perception and sensation. Within this very concentration, there being no consciousness at all, should one wish to leave it, one simply heeds the original interval of time set beforehand, whether long or short.

The eighth detachment's own ten subtle mental factors are a striking piece of phenomenological bookkeeping — even the state traditionally described as "neither perceiving nor not perceiving" is shown to still harbor sensation, perception, formation, contact, intention, desire, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, all operating at a level too fine for the ordinary person to detect. The final move — relinquishing even the concentration and wisdom that were doing the contemplating — is the same self-undermining logic that closed the formless attainments in fascicle 8: no observing position is exempt from being observed and then released in turn, all the way down.

quiz.q: How is the second detachment defined?
options: destroying inner form and its mark, keeping outer form, contemplating it with the impure mind
quiz.why: Destroying inner form and its mark while not destroying outer form, one contemplates outer form with the impure mind.

quiz.q: Having destroyed the inner bones, why does the second detachment still contemplate outer bones as impure?
options: the desire realm's views and thoughts are not yet fully severed
quiz.why: To enter the second dhyāna's inner purity one destroys the inner bones, but since the desire realm's views and thoughts are not fully severed, one still contemplates outer bones.

quiz.q: How do the bones dissolve in the second detachment, and with what does realization arise?
options: the bones crumble like dust into emptiness; samādhi arises with great joy
quiz.why: The bones gradually crumble like dust and return to emptiness; afterward the inner mind opens bright and pure, samādhi arising together with great joy.

quiz.q: In realizing the pure detachment, what of happiness, and how does the fourth dhyāna's pure color differ?
options: happiness arises and pervades the body; the fourth dhyāna lacks the body-pervading happiness
quiz.why: Happiness arises with the concentration and spreads through the whole body; the fourth dhyāna's pure color also belongs to the pure detachment, differing only in lacking body-pervading happiness.

quiz.q: What four senses distinguish the pure detachment?
quiz.why: The four are impure-impure, impure-pure, pure-impure, and pure-pure.

options: bones, originally impure, become white and shining once the grease is gone
quiz.why: White bone is originally impure, but closely contemplated, once the grease is gone, it is like agate and shell, shining white: purity within impurity. B is impure-impure.

quiz.q: What three impure causes affect the pure light from the first detachment onward?
options: its source (the bones), what it illuminates (outer objects), its unrefined substance
quiz.why: The light is impure in its source (issuing from the bones), in what it illuminates (outer objects), and in its unrefined substance.

quiz.q: With what is the unrefined light compared?
options: a later sound stilling an earlier
unrefined gold, its dross not exhausted
quiz.why: Like gold not yet refined, its dross not yet removed, its luster impure.

quiz.q: Why is only the third detachment called the pure detachment?
options: the eight colors are pure and here free of the three impurities, so purity is complete
quiz.why: The eight colors are pure in origin, and here they are freed of the three impurities, so they are pure-pure; the sense of purity being complete, it is called the pure detachment.

quiz.q: How does the means of extinguishing form in the space detachment differ from before?
options: the eight colors depend on mind like illusory forms; when mind relinquishes them they vanish
quiz.why: The eight colors depend on the mind like illusory forms on an illusory mind; when the mind relinquishes them they fade, and one enters boundless space. C is the root method.

quiz.q: What do "deep mind" and "turned wholly one way, never turning back" mean?
options: deep mind is calming; never turning back is insight with emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness
quiz.why: Deep mind is skillful calming; never turning back is skillful insight with emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, relinquishing root attachment so one does not fall back into saṃsāra.

quiz.q: In the formless concentration, what do the first four and last four noble lineages do?
options: antidotes make one weary of the formless; correct contemplations break its two inversions and yield the undefiled
quiz.why: The four antidotes such as boil and wound make one weary of the formless; the four correct contemplations such as impermanence break its provisional and real inversions and yield the undefiled.

quiz.q: How does cultivating the noble lineages in detachment differ from doing so in the root practice?
options: in the root practice one cultivates them to leave space; here at the moment of entering, abiding without attachment
quiz.why: Earlier one cultivated them in order to leave space; here one cultivates them on entering, abiding in concentration without attachment, hence detachment.

quiz.q: Why is the cessation detachment also called "realization in the body"?
options: weary of distraction, disciples rest in a concentration resembling nirvāṇa, settled in the body
quiz.why: Weary of the scattered mind, disciples enter concentration to rest, in a dharma resembling nirvāṇa settled in the body, hence realization in the body.

quiz.q: Which is NOT among the ten subtle mental factors?
quiz.why: The ten are sensation, perception, formation, contact, intention, desire, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom; anger is not among them.

quiz.q: In relinquishing even the sensation and perception that contemplate reality, what simile is used?
options: a later sound stilling an earlier, and then itself being removed
quiz.why: Relinquishing the minds of concentration and wisdom that take reality as object is like using a later sound to still an earlier one; once the earlier has ceased, the later too is removed.

quiz.q: With no consciousness in cessation, how does one emerge?
options: simply according to the duration resolved beforehand
quiz.why: There being no consciousness in it, one emerges simply according to the length of time set beforehand.
